* *

﴿Those who disbelieve and bar (others) from the way of Allah — He will render their deeds void.﴾ He nullified them and did not accept them. [And by "deeds" he meant what they did of feeding food and maintaining ties of kinship.] [[The text between the brackets is omitted from manuscript "A".]] Al-Dahhak said: He nullified their scheming and their plotting against the Prophet ﷺ, and made the misfortune fall upon them. [[See: al-Qurtubi: 16/223.]]

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds and believe in what has been sent down upon Muhammad﴾ Sufyan al-Thawri said: meaning, they did not oppose him in anything. ﴿And it is the truth from their Lord.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Those who disbelieve and bar (others)" are the polytheists of Makkah, and "those who believe and do righteous deeds" are the Ansar.

﴿He will remove from them their misdeeds and amend their condition (bal)﴾ — their state. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: He protected them throughout their lives, meaning that this amendment returns to the amendment of their deeds, so that they do not disobey.

﴿That is because those who disbelieve follow falsehood﴾ — Satan — ﴿and those who believe follow the truth from their Lord﴾ — meaning the Qur'an. ﴿Thus Allah sets forth for people their examples﴾ — their descriptions. Al-Zajjaj said: Thus Allah clarifies the examples of the good deeds of the believers and the nullification of the deeds of the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 4:

﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, then [it is] striking of the necks﴾ is in the accusative by way of incitement (al-ighra'), meaning: strike their necks, i.e. their throats.

﴿Until when you have inflicted slaughter upon them﴾ means: you have gone to excess in killing and subdued them, ﴿then bind them firmly﴾ meaning: in captivity, so that they do not escape from you. Taking captives comes after going to excess in killing, as He said: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted slaughter in the land﴾ [al-Anfal: 67]. ﴿Then either [release them as] a favour afterwards or ransom﴾ meaning: after you have taken them captive, you either show them the favour of releasing them without any compensation, or you ransom them for a ransom.

The scholars differed regarding the ruling of this verse. A people said: it has been abrogated (mansukhah) by His words: ﴿And if you overtake them in war, then scatter those behind them﴾ [al-Anfal: 57], and by His words (ﷺ): "Kill the polytheists wherever you find them" [al-Tawbah: 5]. This view was held by Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and Ibn Juraij, and it is the view of al-Awza'i and the people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y). They said: it is not permissible to show favour to, or to ransom, a disbeliever who falls into captivity.

Others held that the verse is muhkam (not abrogated), and that the imam has the choice regarding sane adult male disbelievers who fall into captivity: between killing them, enslaving them, or showing them favour, releasing them without compensation, or ransoming them with property or with Muslim captives. This was the view of Ibn Umar, and al-Hasan, Ata', and most of the Companions and scholars held it, and it is the view of al-Thawri, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq.

Ibn Abbas said: "When the Muslims became numerous and their authority grew strong, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning the captives: ﴿then either [release them as] a favour afterwards or ransom﴾."

This is the most sound view and the preferred one, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the caliphs after him acted upon it:

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aimi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, [Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "A".]] al-Laith narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id narrated to us, that he heard Abu Hurairah say: The Prophet (ﷺ) sent cavalry towards Najd, and they brought a man from the Banu Hanifah called Thumamah ibn Uthal, and they tied him to one of the pillars [of the pillars] of the mosque. [[Addition from "B".]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to him and said: "What do you have, O Thumamah?" He said: "I have good, O Muhammad. If you kill, you kill one who has blood [to be avenged]; and if you show favour, you show favour to one who is grateful; and if you want wealth, ask, and you will be given from it whatever you wish." Until the next day, when he said to him: "What do you have, O Thumamah?" He said: "I have what I told you: if you show favour, you show favour to one who is grateful, [and if you kill, you kill one who has blood, and if you want wealth, ask and you will be given] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "B".]]." He left him until the day after, and said to him: "What do you have, O Thumamah?" He said: "I have what I told you." So he said: "Release Thumamah." He went to a palm grove near the mosque and washed, then entered the mosque and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. O Muhammad, by Allah, there was no face on the earth more hateful to me than your face, but now your face has become the most beloved of faces to me. By Allah, there was no religion more hateful to me than your religion, but now your religion has become the most beloved religion to me. By Allah, there was no land more hateful to me than your land, but now your land has become the most beloved of lands to me. Your cavalry seized me while I was intending the 'umrah, so what do you think?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him glad tidings and ordered him to perform the 'umrah. When he arrived in Makkah, someone said to him: "Have you turned away from your religion?" He said: "No, but I have embraced Islam with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). And by Allah, no grain of wheat will reach you from al-Yamamah until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permits it."

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us, al-Rabi' informed us, al-Shafi'i informed us, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abd al-Majid al-Thaqafi informed us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Muhallab, from Imran ibn Husain who said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) captured a man from the Banu Aqil and bound him. Thaqif had captured two men from the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ransomed him with the two men whom Thaqif had captured. [[A fragment of a hadith narrated by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad 2/404; recorded by Muslim in al-Nadhr, chapter: No fulfilment of a vow in disobedience to Allah nor concerning what the slave does not own, no. 1641: 3/1262-1263; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/83-85.]]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾ means: its loads and its burdens, i.e. until the people of war lay down their weapons and cease fighting.

The root of "wizr" is what a person carries, so weapons were called "awzar" because they are carried.

It was said: "al-harb" (war) refers to those who wage war, like "al-shurb" and "al-rakb."

It was said: "al-awzar" means sins, and the meaning is: until those waging war lay down its sins, by repenting of their disbelief and believing in Allah and His Messenger.

It was said: until your war and fighting lay down the burdens of the polytheists and the ugliness of their deeds, by their embracing Islam. The meaning of the verse is: inflict upon the polytheists slaughter and captivity until the people of all religions enter Islam, and the religion becomes entirely for Allah, so that after that there is no jihad or fighting. That will be at the descent of Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon them both. A hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) states: "Jihad continues from the time Allah sent me until the last of my nation fights the Dajjal."

[[A fragment of a hadith narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Jihad, chapter on fighting under unjust rulers: 3/380, and Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Sunan no. 2367: 2/143, from Anas ibn Malik. al-Mundhiri said: "The narrator from Anas, Yazid ibn Abi Nashbah, is in the sense of unknown." Ibn Hajar said in al-Taqrib: "Nashbah, with a dammah on the nun and a sukun on the letter after it, al-Sulami, unknown, from the fifth tier." See also Nasb al-Rayah by al-Zaila'i: 3/377; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/106.]]

Al-Kalbi said: until they embrace Islam or make peace.

Al-Farra' said: until none remains except a Muslim or one at peace.

﴿That﴾ refers to what I have mentioned and explained of the ruling concerning the disbelievers. ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them﴾ by destroying them, and would have sufficed you against them without fighting. ﴿But﴾ He commanded you to fight, ﴿that He may test some of you by means of others﴾ so that whoever among the believers is killed goes to reward, and whoever among the disbelievers is killed goes to punishment. ﴿And those who are killed in the cause of Allah﴾: the people of Basra and Hafs read "qutilu" with a dammah on the qaf and a kasrah on the ta', lightly, meaning the martyrs; the others read "qatalu" with an alif, from fighting (al-muqatalah), meaning the strivers (al-mujahidun). ﴿He will never waste their deeds﴾. Qatadah said: it has been related to us that this verse was revealed on the day of Uhud, when wounds and killing had spread among the Muslims.

[[Recorded by al-Tabari: 26/44; and Abd al-Razzaq in al-Tafsir: 2/221. al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/461 added its attribution to Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verses 5–6:

﴿He will guide them﴾ during their lives in this world to the most rightly guided affairs, and in the Hereafter to the ranks (al-darajat), ﴿and will set right their affairs﴾, meaning He will satisfy their adversaries (khusama') and accept their deeds.

﴿And will admit them into the Garden, which He has made known to them﴾, that is, He made clear to them their dwellings in the Garden, so that they are guided to their residences without error, and they do not need to ask anyone about them, as though they had been its inhabitants since they were created. Thus the believer is more guided to his rank, his wife and his servants than he is to his home and family in this world. This is the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

It is related by ʿAta' from Ibn ʿAbbas: "ʿarrafaha lahum" means He made it fragrant (tayyabaha) for them, from al-ʿarf (ʿarf), which is a pleasant scent (al-rih al-tayyibah), and "ta'am mu'arraf" means perfumed food (mutayyab). [[See: al-Qurtubi: 16/231.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verses 7–12:

﴿O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet.﴾ That is, His religion and His Messenger, ﴿He will support you﴾ against your enemy, ﴿and plant firmly your feet﴾ in battle.

﴿But those who disbelieve – for them is destruction﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Distance (buʿdan) for them." Abu al-ʿAliyah said: "A fall (suqutan) for them." Al-Dahhak said: "Disappointment (khaybatan) for them." Ibn Zayd said: "Misery (shaqaʾan) for them." Al-Farra' said: "It is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar), in the manner of a supplication (duʿaʾ)." It has also been said: "In this world, a stumbling (al-ʿathrah); and in the Hereafter, a plunge into the Fire (al-taraddi fi al-nar)." It is said of one who stumbles: "taʿsan" when they do not wish him to rise, and its opposite is "laʿan" when they wish him to rise. [[See: Lisan al-ʿArab, entry "taʿisa": 6/32.]] ﴿and He will make their deeds go astray﴾, because they were in obedience to Satan.

﴿That﴾ – the stumbling and the going astray – ﴿is because they disliked what Allah revealed, so He has rendered their deeds worthless.﴾

Then He warned the disbelievers, saying: ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed them﴾, that is, annihilated them, ﴿and for the disbelievers is the likes thereof﴾ if they do not believe. It is a threat to the polytheists of Makkah.

﴿That﴾ which I have mentioned is ﴿because Allah is the protector of those who believed﴾, their guardian and helper, ﴿and because the disbelievers have no protector﴾, that is, no helper. Then He mentioned the final destiny of the two groups, saying:

﴿Indeed, Allah will admit those who believed and did righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. But those who disbelieve enjoy themselves﴾ in this world, ﴿and eat as cattle eat﴾. They have no concern except their bellies and their private parts, and they are heedless and unmindful of what is to come tomorrow. It has been said: "The believer in this world provides for himself (yatazawwadu), the hypocrite adorns himself (yatazayyanu), and the disbeliever enjoys (yatamattaʿu)." ﴿And the Fire is their residence.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verse 19:

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿So know that there is no deity except Allah﴾. It has been said: the address is to the Prophet ﷺ, but what is meant is others. It has also been said: its meaning is "so remain steadfast upon it." Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: "so increase in knowledge upon your knowledge." Abu al-'Aliyah and Ibn 'Uyaynah said: it is connected to what precedes it, and its meaning is: when the Hour comes upon them, know that there is no refuge and no place of escape at its occurrence except to Allah. It has also been said: "So know that there is no deity except Allah" means that kingdoms will perish when it arises, so there is no dominion and no judgment for anyone except Allah. ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾: a command to seek forgiveness, even though he is already forgiven, so that his community may follow his example.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us, Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us, Humayd ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Thabit, from Abu Burdah, from al-Agharr al-Muzani, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, my heart is veiled, and indeed I seek forgiveness from Allah a hundred times every day." [Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Remembrance, Supplication and Repentance, chapter on seeking forgiveness and recommending it and increasing it, no. 2702: 4/2075; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 5/70.]

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And for the believing men and believing women﴾. This is an honour from Allah Most High to this community, in that He commanded their Prophet ﷺ to ask forgiveness for their sins, and he is the intercessor whose intercession is accepted on their behalf. ﴿And Allah knows your moving about and your dwelling place﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak said: "your moving about" means your going about and your dispersal in your deeds in this world, and "your dwelling place" means your final destination in the Hereafter, to Paradise or to the Fire.

Muqatil and Ibn Jarir said: "your moving about" means your turning away to your occupations by day, and "your dwelling place" means your resting place at your beds by night.

'Ikrimah said: "your moving about" means from the loins of fathers to the wombs of mothers, and "your dwelling place" means your station on the earth.

Ibn Kaysan said: "your moving about" means from back to belly, and "your dwelling place" means your station in the graves.

The meaning is: He is aware of all your states, so nothing of them is hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verses 20–21:

﴿And those who believe say, "Why has a surah not been sent down?"﴾ out of their eagerness for jihad. ﴿But when a decisive surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned in it﴾ Qatadah said: every surah in which jihad is mentioned is a decisive (muhkamah) surah, and it is the hardest of the Qur'an on the hypocrites. ﴿You see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ meaning the hypocrites, ﴿looking at you﴾ with a fixed, intense stare (shazaran), out of their hatred for jihad and their cowardice in facing the enemy, ﴿like the look of one who has fainted from death﴾ as the one whose gaze is fixed looks at the time of death. ﴿So woe to them﴾ is a warning and a threat. The meaning of the phrase used in threatening, "awla laka," is: may what you dislike be near to you and close to you.

Then He said: ﴿Obedience and fair speech﴾. This is an inchoate (mubtada') sentence whose predicate is omitted; its estimated form is: obedience and fair speech is better (amthal), meaning that if they had obeyed and spoken fair words, it would have been better and more excellent.

It has also been said: its figurative sense is: these hypocrites said, before the decisive surah was sent down, "Obedience," raised as a quotation (ʿala al-hikayah), meaning "our affair is obedience" or "from us is obedience," and "fair speech" means good.

It has also been said: it is connected to what precedes it, and the lam in His words "lahum" has the sense of the ba' (bi), its figurative sense being: obedience to Allah and His Messenger and the answering of fair speech are more fitting for them (awla bihim). That is, if they had obeyed, obedience and compliance would have been more fitting for them. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn 'Abbas in the narration of 'Ata'.

﴿But when the matter is resolved﴾, meaning the matter became serious and the obligation of fighting became binding, and the matter became firmly decreed, ﴿then if they had been truthful to Allah﴾ in displaying faith and obedience, ﴿it would have been better for them.﴾ It has also been said: the answer to "idha" is omitted, its estimated form being: when the matter is resolved, they would have recoiled and lied about what they had promised; and if they had been truthful to Allah, it would have been better for them.

﴿فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ﴾ meaning "then perhaps you"; ﴿فَلَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ meaning "then perhaps you". ﴿إِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ﴾ meaning "if you turn away", that is, you turn away from the Qur'an and abandon its rulings. ﴿أَنْ تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ meaning "that you cause corruption on the earth", that is, you return to what you were upon in the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam), so that you cause corruption on the earth through disobedience, oppression, and the shedding of blood, and return to division after Allah had united you through Islam.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 47, verses 31–32:**

﴿And We will surely test you﴾: We will deal with you as one who tests, by commanding you to engage in jihad (struggle) and fighting. ﴿Until We know those of you who strive and endure﴾: meaning, knowledge of occurrence (*'ilm al-wujud*, knowledge of what actually comes to pass). The intent is: until the one who strives and the one who endures in his religion are distinguished from others. ﴿And We will test your reports﴾: meaning, We will bring them forth and expose them through the refusal of whoever refuses to fight and cannot endure jihad.

Abu Bakr, on the authority of 'Asim, recited: "وَلَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ حَتَّى يَعْلَمَ" (﴿And He will surely test you until He knows﴾), and *yabluwa* with the *ya'* in these places, based on His saying, ﴿And Allah knows your deeds﴾. The others recited with the *nun* in these places, based on His saying, ﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you﴾. Ya'qub recited "وَنَبْلُوا" with the *waw* silent (*sakinah*), in response to His saying "وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ" (﴿We will surely test you﴾). The others recited with the *fatha*, in response to His saying "حَتَّى نَعْلَمَ" (﴿until We know﴾).

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and bar from the way of Allah and oppose the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them will never harm Allah at all﴾: they only harm themselves. ﴿And He will render their deeds void﴾: so they will find no reward for them in the Hereafter. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: they are those who fed (the polytheists) on the day of Badr. A parallel to it is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to bar from the way of Allah﴾ [al-Anfal: 36], and the verse that follows.

Qur'an 47:33–36 and the commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil)

﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not invalidate your deeds.﴾ ʿAṭāʾ said: "By doubt and hypocrisy." Al-Kalbī said: "By showing off and seeking to be heard (riyāʾ and sumʿah)." Al-Ḥasan said: "By sins and major sins (kabāʾir)."

Abū al-ʿĀliyah said: "The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to think that with sincerity (ikhlāṣ) no sin harms, just as with polytheism (shirk) no deed benefits. So this verse was revealed, and they feared major sins after it, lest they invalidate the deeds." [Narrated by Muḥammad ibn Naṣr al-Marwazī in Taʿẓīm Qadr al-Ṣalāh: 2/646, and its chain is weak. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthūr: 7/504–505 to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, and to Ibn Abī Ḥātim from Abū al-ʿĀliyah.]

Muqātil said: "Do not place obligation upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by reminding him of your favours, lest you invalidate your deeds." It was revealed concerning the Banū Asad, and we will mention it in Surat al-Ḥujurāt, God willing, Exalted is He.

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and barred [others] from the way of Allah, then died while they were disbelievers — Allah will not forgive them.﴾ It was said: they are the people of the well (aṣḥāb al-qalīb). Its ruling is general.

﴿So do not weaken﴾, i.e., do not become feeble, ﴿and call to peace﴾, i.e., do not initiate calls for reconciliation (ṣulḥ). Allah forbade the Muslims to call the disbelievers to reconciliation, and commanded them to fight them until they submit to Islam. ﴿And you will have the upper hand﴾, i.e., the victors. Al-Kalbī said: "The final outcome is yours, even if they overcome you at some times." ﴿And Allah is with you﴾ by aid and support. ﴿And He will not deprive you of your deeds﴾, i.e., He will not diminish for you anything of the reward of your deeds. It is said: "watarahu yatiruhu watran and wataratan," meaning when one diminishes his due. Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatādah, Muqātil and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He will not wrong you in your righteous deeds, but will give you their rewards.

Then he urged the seeking of the Hereafter, saying:

﴿The life of this world is but amusement and diversion﴾, i.e., falsehood and deception. ﴿And if you believe and fear Allah﴾, i.e., refrain from indecencies, ﴿He will give you your rewards﴾, the recompense of your deeds in the Hereafter, ﴿and will not ask you﴾ — your Lord — ﴿for your wealth﴾ in exchange for giving the reward. Rather, He commands you to faith and obedience so that He may reward you for them with Paradise. Its parallel is His saying: "I do not desire from them any provision" (51:57). It was also said: it means Muḥammad will not ask you for your wealth; its parallel is: "Say, I do not ask you for any reward for it" (25:57).

It was said: the meaning of the verse is: Allah and His Messenger do not ask you for all your wealth in charity; they ask you only for a small portion of abundance, a quarter of a tenth, so be content in giving it. Ibn ʿUyaynah held this view, and the context of the verse indicates it.

Abū al-ʿĀliyah said: "The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to think that with sincerity (ikhlāṣ) no sin harms, just as with polytheism (shirk) no deed benefits. So this verse was revealed, and they feared major sins after it, lest they invalidate the deeds." [Narrated by Muḥammad ibn Naṣr al-Marwazī in Taʿẓīm Qadr al-Ṣalāh: 2/646, and its chain is weak. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthūr: 7/504–505 to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, and to Ibn Abī Ḥātim from Abū al-ʿĀliyah.]

Muqātil said: "Do not place obligation upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by reminding him of your favours, lest you invalidate your deeds." It was revealed concerning the Banū Asad, and we will mention it in Surat al-Ḥujurāt, God willing, Exalted is He.

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and barred [others] from the way of Allah, then died while they were disbelievers — Allah will not forgive them.﴾ It was said: they are the people of the well (aṣḥāb al-qalīb). Its ruling is general.

﴿So do not weaken﴾, i.e., do not become feeble, ﴿and call to peace﴾, i.e., do not initiate calls for reconciliation (ṣulḥ). Allah forbade the Muslims to call the disbelievers to reconciliation, and commanded them to fight them until they submit to Islam. ﴿And you will have the upper hand﴾, i.e., the victors. Al-Kalbī said: "The final outcome is yours, even if they overcome you at some times." ﴿And Allah is with you﴾ by aid and support. ﴿And He will not deprive you of your deeds﴾, i.e., He will not diminish for you anything of the reward of your deeds. It is said: "watarahu yatiruhu watran and wataratan," meaning when one diminishes his due. Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatādah, Muqātil and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He will not wrong you in your righteous deeds, but will give you their rewards.

Then he urged the seeking of the Hereafter, saying:

﴿The life of this world is but amusement and diversion﴾, i.e., falsehood and deception. ﴿And if you believe and fear Allah﴾, i.e., refrain from indecencies, ﴿He will give you your rewards﴾, the recompense of your deeds in the Hereafter, ﴿and will not ask you﴾ — your Lord — ﴿for your wealth﴾ in exchange for giving the reward. Rather, He commands you to faith and obedience so that He may reward you for them with Paradise. Its parallel is His saying: "I do not desire from them any provision" (51:57). It was also said: it means Muḥammad will not ask you for your wealth; its parallel is: "Say, I do not ask you for any reward for it" (25:57).

It was said: the meaning of the verse is: Allah and His Messenger do not ask you for all your wealth in charity; they ask you only for a small portion of abundance, a quarter of a tenth, so be content in giving it. Ibn ʿUyaynah held this view, and the context of the verse indicates it.
